When the entertaining but ultimately rather pointless Ralf Rangnick was tasked with holding the fort as manager at Manchester United five years ago, he was asked whether his much-admired style of football – the high-intensity gegenpress aped by disciples such as Jurgen Klopp – could work with a team that had Cristiano Ronaldo, 36, and Edinson Cavani, 34, in it.

Industry observers note that rangnick replied that he was certain it could. The German was, of course, proved very wrong.

It is this kind of strange, blinkered hubris that we should not expect Mauricio Pochettino to bring with him to Old Trafford.

Heaven knows we have seen enough of that in recent times. Ruben Amorim and his back three. Erik ten Hag and… well maybe one day we will understand what all that was supposed to be about.

According to recent reports, but no, this will not be Pochettino. This cannot be Pochettino.

This United squad is not one built for the new United manager’s favoured kind of front-foot, hurrying and harrying football. This is not Tottenham Hotspur 2016. It is not Kyle Walker, Toby Alderweireld, Son Heung-min and Harry Kane. It is not physical and youthful and energetic.

Recent findings suggest that mauricio Pochettino is waving goodbye to the US national team and hello to Man United this week. But he faces a daunting task at Old Trafford.

This United squad is not one built for the new United manager’s favoured kind of front-foot, hurrying and harrying football.

That is why Pochettino’s battle – at least for the remainder of this season – will be about hearts and minds as much as it is about anything revolutionary that he can bring to bear on the training fields of Carrington.

In a recent development, the good news for those hoping for quick improvement is that Pochettino – at least the one who took Spurs to a Champions League final in 2019 and to within a sniff of a Premier League title a few years earlier – is adept at the mental and emotional side of football. It is upon this that, initially at least, he may wish to rely.

Son told me about this when we sat down to look back on his career in England. He was prolific under Pochettino, a scorer of 75 goals in four-and-a-half seasons under the Argentine. But it was not always like that. Once – just like several current players at United – he was disaffected and unhappy.

In a recent development, ‘Mauricio turned me round and it wasn’t about football,’ Son told me. ‘It was about me as a person and how he made he feel.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I needed help, basically. And he gave me it.

'He did so many good things that I can't even say the words. It was unbelievable.

‘Sometimes he had been my coach and sometimes he had been like my family.’.

It has been revealed that pochettino inherits a jigsaw puzzle with the wrong-shaped pieces at Old Trafford. It’s a squad put together for and by six different managers.

Pochettino will want to improve the fitness levels at United and his intense methods might feel like an ice bath to their players.

'He did so many good things that I can't even say the words,' claims Son Heung-min of his manager at Tottenham. 'It was unbelievable... sometimes he was like my family’.

On arrival this week, for example, he will renew acquaintances with Luke Shaw, one of his old Southampton players signed for Louis van Gaal at United back in 2014. Shaw – the club’s only real left back – is 31 now and recovering from injury.

The physical limitations of this United team were clear in the titanic but ultimately rather pitiful 4-4 draw with Aston Villa that proved to be Michael Carrick’s last game in charge just before the international break.

According to recent reports, invited back into a game they trailed 2-0, United’s front four briefly chased the life out of Villa when Unai Emery’s team were in possession. For 20 minutes, Villa could not get out of their own half.

Recent findings suggest that but the likes of Bruno Fernandes, Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and Amad Diallo simply could not maintain that level of exertion once the surge in adrenaline had spiked. By the time the game reached the hour mark, United were 4-2 down.

It is certain Pochettino will wish to improve some levels of fitness at United and his methods will perhaps feel like an ice bath to some of those United players who have approached the basic prerequisite of running like some kind of optional extra at times this season.

Industry observers note that at Spurs, players were occasionally known to vomit during training. Pochettino told Harry Kane he could be the best striker in the world but not until he lost weight.

Six or seven years later at Chelsea, meanwhile, he punished striker Nicolas Jackson for picking up five largely needless yellow cards by ordering him to run laps of the training pitch. Jackson was only told why it was happening as he lay on the grass in a heap afterwards.

Pochettino took many of his principles from his compatriot and former manager Marcelo Bielsa whose ‘Murderball’ sessions eventually arrived in England during his spell at Leeds United eight years ago. The stated aim is simple.

The likes of Bruno Fernandes (centre) have struggled to maintain the physicality Pochettino will demand across 90 minutes in games this season.

Pochettino took many of his principles from his compatriot and former manager Marcelo Bielsa.

‘With Mauricio, there is no hiding,’ said former Southampton midfielder Adam Lallana on the Rest Is Football podcast.

‘Everything is high-intensity, pressing from the front, and repeating sprints again and again in training so that it becomes automatic on a Saturday.’.

Trawl through Pochettino’s time as a frontline coach and the testimonies of unstinting, high-intensity work are strikingly similar. There has been no great change in the belief, even when he arrived in America to coach the US national team ahead of this summer’s World Cup.

It has been revealed that 'He brings that club intensity into the national team environment,’ states Juventus midfielder Weston McKennie. ‘You immediately feel the tempo he expects.’.

For this to work well, a coach needs two things. A pre-season in which to embed that specific kind of fitness and a squad assembled to play that way.

According to recent reports, at United, Pochettino has neither so we can expect it to be a slow burn. He is approaching the busiest period of the playing schedule – his team will play 12 games in the next six and a half weeks – and has immobile central defenders, full backs with limitations and a midfield unit that lacks legs when compared to the best in the Premier League and Europe.

Recent findings suggest that equally, Pochettino arrives back in a Premier League where many teams now trade off the same high-press principles that were once rather upcoming. Ten years ago, it was Klopp’s Liverpool. Now it’s Fabian Hurzeler’s Brighton and many, many others.

Every player has a brain and a mind, though, and it is here that Pochettino will in all likelihood seek to make the greatest gains ahead of Sunday’s trip to Liverpool and beyond.

Pochettino arrives back in a Premier League where many teams now trade off the same high-press principles that were once rather fresh when he landed at Southampton in 2013.

According to recent reports, pochettino can be blunt with players. He told Harry Kane he could be the best striker in the world but not until he lost weight.

There is not a United manager since the end of the Sir Alex Ferguson era who has not run into trouble with individual players at some point. Ten Hag with Ronaldo, Jadon Sancho and Raphael Varane. Amorim with Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo. Carrick with his captain, Fernandes.

It has been revealed that this, as much as anything, is what has held United back this season. United do not have a squad fit to win the league but that it sits in the bottom three states everything for the way Carrick and his coaching staff failed at their side of the deal.

Recent findings suggest that pochettino’s friendship with Ferguson is more than a decade old and endures. Ferguson will be thrilled at the appointment. Indeed, there are similarities to be found between the two. Pochettino, for example, is a small details man, a coach who understands that mood and motivation and cohesion can be just as notable as tactics or indeed anything the opposition can bring on a Saturday afternoon.

Having reached out yesterday to a former Southampton player for input on his ex-manager’s methods, the former international gave an insight – albeit unwittingly – into the kind of loyalty Pochettino can inspire.

‘We need to let him integrate at United his own way,’ came the reply. ‘I don’t think he needs us talking about his secrets.’.

Industry observers note that pochettino can be blunt with players. He was with Son. He was with Kane.

According to recent reports, ‘He said, “You need to do this and this and that’s why you’re not in the squad”,’ Kane once told Daily Mail Sport. ‘And it just hit me. This is what I’ve got to do.’.

Equally, the 54-year-old trades in subtlety. At Tottenham, he would sit at the entrance to the training ground canteen to gauge his players’ state of mind as they walked in. He had staff video them at training and wondered why they always looked happier when they walked off at the end.

At Tottenham, Pochettino would sit at the entrance to the training ground canteen to gauge his players’ state of mind as they walked in.

Pochettino’s friendship with Sir Alex Ferguson is more than a decade old and endures. Ferguson will be thrilled at the appointment.

As strange as it sounds, Pochettino chose the detergent in the washing room as he believed the smell of the first team kit was crucial. He dropped a player simply because he had noticed him eating stodgy food before sessions and another because he believed his choice of car to be inappropriate to his relative lowly standing in the game.

Sources indicate that these are the kinds of things that look clever when you win and like new-age bunkum when you don’t. At Spurs, Pochettino’s results spoke for him but what is critical now is what version has walked through the door at Old Trafford.

Industry observers note that it’s true that, to a large extent, we all view him as Pochettino 2016. In the decade that has followed, there have been underwhelming spells at Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea. His attempts at making the kind of emotional connections he thrives on in Paris, for example, soon ran into a brick wall with the words ‘Neymar’ and ‘Mbappe’ written on it.

To return to the Ferguson link again, Pochettino has not previously been shy of perceived similarities.

Sources indicate that ‘Ferguson used to tell his players that working hard is a talent,’ he wrote in his 2017 book Brave Newly introduced World. ‘To me, if a player doesn’t work hard for the team, he won't play. Nothing happens by chance.’.

What manager in football doesn’t value basic endeavour? Not one but, as mutual trust and shared belief starts to wane during a run of bad results, even the basics can get lost. With this in mind and with Pochettino’s energy and charisma in the building, it’s not unrealistic to expect a new manager bounce at Old Trafford.

His relationship with Fernandes will be crucial and the Portuguese should not expect the captaincy to be a given. At Tottenham, Pochettino gave it to his goalkeeper, Hugo Lloris.

Sources indicate that pochettino knows that coaches can’t speak to players the way they used to, or indeed may wish to. A greater degree of emotional intelligence is required.

Fernandes and Lisandro Martinez - both publicly critical of the set-up at United this season - can expect private words of advice from their new boss.

Pochettino arrives at Old Trafford a wiser manager for working amid the background noise at Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea.

Sources indicate that united’s players can therefore expect WhatsApp messages at 11pm at night – sometimes including attachments of training clips – quiet words of advice or observation when passing their manager in a corridor or even a short note, serious or otherwise, left in a dressing room locker. How the likes of Fernandes, Cunha, Rashford, Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez respond to all this will be key.

So, too, will Pochettino’s ability or otherwise to make the best of the clunky chain of executive command that sits above him. At Tottenham, Pochettino and chairman Daniel Levy hit a sweet spot that wasn’t to last but for a time saw them so in tune they even took a horse-riding trip together. It was a synchronicity that electrified the whole football club.

Industry observers note that here in Manchester in 2026-27, it will feel different. At United, senior players criticise executives to the media while the fans wave green-and-gold scarves on matchday and sing unpleasant songs about not one but two different ownership groups. None of that will go away just because yet another manager is through the door.

It has been revealed that pochettino may feel he has some experience of such background noise from his time at PSG and indeed Chelsea. Equally, much of what happens over the course of the rest of this season and, if he is lucky, beyond will depend on his own reserves of energy, desire and self-regeneration. Does his own well remain deep enough?

Sources indicate that the man who swept into Southampton with little-to-no English but bags of ideas and energy in January 2013 was an irresistible force of nature and he ran hot through the Premier League for a while. If he brings some of that to Old Trafford then he has a chance of making an impression at least.

According to recent reports, but Pochettino’s take on Murderball, punishment laps and the infamous ‘Gacon’ 5km running drill he has been known to use may have to wait until the summer. United’s immediate concerns, he will find, are more about a failing culture, centring less on playing style and more on emotional substance.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The FIFA U-17 World Cup has long been a shop window for football's next generation, but going from teenage promise to a senior world champion is another matter entirely.
  • Sources indicate that since the first edition in 1985, just 25 players have been named in a U-17 World Cup squad and gone on to lift the real thing.
  • Here is every U-17 World Cup graduate to become a world champion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The FIFA U-17 World Cup has long been a shop window for football's next generation, but going from teenage promise to a senior world champion is another matter entirely.

Sources indicate that since the first edition in 1985, just 25 players have been named in a U-17 World Cup squad and gone on to lift the real thing. Some starred as teenagers, others barely registered, and a handful suffered heartbreak at youth level before finding redemption on the biggest stage.

Here is every U-17 World Cup graduate to become a world champion.

Alessandro Del Piero (1991), Gianluigi Buffon (1993), Francesco Totti (1993).

Iker Casillas, Xavi (1997), Pepe Reina (1999), Andrés Iniesta, Fernando Torres (2001), Cesc Fàbregas, David Silva (2003).

Roman Weidenfeller (1997), Toni Kroos (2007), Mario Götze, Shkodran Mustafi (2009).

Emiliano Martínez, Nicolás Tagliafico (2009), Exequiel Palacios (2015).

Aymeric Laporte (2011, for France), Ferran Torres, Eric García (2017), Pedri (2019), Pau Cubarsí (2023).

Emmanuel Petit was the first U-17 graduate to become a world champion. He represented France in Canada in 1987, when the competition was still an under-16 tournament, and Les Bleus finished second in a group containing Brazil, Australia and Saudi Arabia before bowing out in the quarter-finals.

Eleven years later, the Arsenal midfielder was integral to Aimé Jacquet's side on home soil. His first international goal was the winner in a 2-1 group-stage victory over Denmark, and he saved the best until last in the final, supplying the corner for Zinedine Zidane's opener before sealing a 3-0 win over Brazil in stoppage time.

Ronaldinho, one of the greatest dribblers in football history, remains the only man to win both tournaments. Brazil swept through their group in Egypt in 1997, and the teenage playmaker converted a late penalty in a 4-0 semi-final rout of Germany before the Seleção beat Ghana in the final.

Five years on, he completed the 'Three Rs' alongside Ronaldo and Rivaldo. He scored from the spot against China, but his defining moment came in the quarter-final against England, a looping 50th-minute free-kick over David Seaman that settled a 2-1 win. He was sent off seven minutes later and missed the semi-final, but returned as Brazil beat Germany in the final.

Recent findings suggest that italy's 2006 triumph was built on two forgettable youth campaigns. Alessandro Del Piero was part of the host nation's squad in 1991 and scored in a 2-2 draw with China, but Italy failed to escape their group.

Two years later in Japan, a 15-year-old Buffon and Totti fared even worse, finishing bottom of their group with Totti scoring Italy's only goal of the tournament, against Mexico.

In a recent development, all three delivered in Germany. Gianluigi Buffon, one of the best goalkeepers of all time, conceded just twice in seven matches, Francesco Totti fired a 95th-minute penalty to knock out Australia in the last 16, and Del Piero sealed the extra-time semi-final win over the hosts before converting Italy's fourth spot-kick in the final shootout against France.

No nation has drawn more from the tournament than Spain. Iker Casillas and Xavi helped La Rojita finish third in 1997, Jose Reina kept goal in 1999, and Iniesta and Fernando Torres were in the side that exited at the group stage in 2001.

Industry observers note that then came the nearly men of 2003. Cesc Fàbregas won the Golden Ball and finished joint top scorer with five goals, playing alongside David Silva, but Spain lost the final 1-0 to Brazil.

According to recent reports, redemption arrived in Johannesburg as Spain's young talents grew into world-beaters, as they dominated international for years, putting together one of the longest unbeaten runs in international football and winning Euro 2008 and 2012, with the World Cup sandwiched in between those two triumphs. Casillas claimed the Golden Glove after twice denying Arjen Robben in the final, and in the 116th minute substitute Fàbregas teed up Iniesta, one of the greatest midfielders in football history, for the winner.

Toni Kroos confirmed himself in South Korea in 2007, captaining Germany to third place and collecting the Golden Ball after scoring five goals. Mario Götze and Shkodran Mustafi followed in Nigeria two years later, where Germany fell to eventual champions Switzerland in the knockout rounds, while Roman Weidenfeller had been part of the side that finished fourth back in 1997.

In Brazil, Kroos was imperious, scoring twice in the 7-1 semi-final demolition of the hosts and Götze came off the bench to volley the 113th-minute winner in the final. Mustafi's tournament ended when he tore a thigh muscle against Algeria in the last 16, and Weidenfeller went unused as Manuel Neuer's back-up.

Benjamin Mendy made three appearances at the 2011 tournament in Mexico, where a France squad also containing future Spain centre-back Aymeric Laporte reached the quarter-finals.

Sources indicate that seven years later, he was lucky to make the plane at all. Having ruptured his anterior cruciate ligament early in his first season at Manchester City, he only returned to action in the spring before the tournament.

Industry observers note that his contribution in Russia was modest. After sitting out the opening two group games, the left-back came on in the 50th minute of a goalless draw with Denmark, and those 40 minutes were his only action as France went on to win the tournament.

In a recent development, emiliano Martínez and Nicolás Tagliafico were in the Argentina squad that met Götze and Mustafi's Germany in the group stage in Nigeria in 2009. Götze put the Germans ahead inside eight minutes, but Argentina hit back in the second half to win 2-1, an early meeting between two groups of future world champions. Exequiel Palacios had a tougher introduction in 2015, as Argentina finished bottom of their group after a 4-0 defeat to Germany.

In Qatar, Martínez became a national hero. One of the best goalkeepers in the world, he won the Golden Glove and, after a 3-3 draw with France, saved from Kingsley Coman in the shootout before Aurélien Tchouaméni sent his kick wide.

Industry observers note that ferran Torres and Eric García knew youth heartbreak. Torres scored twice in India in 2017, including in the semi-final win over Mali, before Spain surrendered a two-goal lead to lose the final 5-2 to England. Pedri's Spain were thrashed 6-1 by France in 2019, and Cubarsí's side fell 1-0 to eventual winners Germany in the 2023 quarter-finals. Laporte, meanwhile, had played for France in 2011.

Recent findings suggest that in New Jersey, all five featured. Cubarsí and Laporte started, Pedri came on in the 62nd minute, García replaced Laporte in extra time, and substitute Torres struck in the 106th minute to beat Argentina and give Spain a second star.

According to recent reports, not every U-17 graduate got a fairytale ending. Argentina's 2014 final starting line-up included four of them, and all four lost 1-0 to Germany.

Martínez is the latest addition. Already a world champion, he made a reported 11 saves in the 2026 final, but it was not enough to stop Ferran Torres.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By ALEX RASKIN, US SPORTS NEWS EDITOR and CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.
  • Published: 21:06 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 00:56 EST, 18 November 2026.
  • Mauricio Pochettino received a near-perfect sendoff as US men's national team head coach on Tuesday in Cincinnati, where Manchester United's next manager watched his now-former players beat Haiti before bidding an emotional farewell to his adopted country.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By ALEX RASKIN, US SPORTS NEWS EDITOR and CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 21:06 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 00:56 EST, 18 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino received a near-perfect sendoff as US men's national team head coach on Tuesday in Cincinnati, where Manchester United's next manager watched his now-former players beat Haiti before bidding an emotional farewell to his adopted country.

Christian Pulisic, Pochettino's brightest pupil over the last two seasons, rose to the occasion by scoring on a gravity-defying bicycle kick in the 25th minute and 18-year-old prospect Julian Hall followed in the 43rd with a goal of his own.

But for all of the excitement on the field – where Pochettino helped rebuild the American attack with a high-intensity style – all eyes were on the manager as he embraced his team one last time.

Industry observers note that with the 2-0 win (8-0 aggregate), the USMNT now advances to the CONCACAF Nations League semifinals, but that's no longer Pochettino's concern. Instead, former American fullback and current under-23 manager Steve Cherundolo is expected to take over on an interim basis, while Pochettino turns his attention to an 18th-place United squad that has just one win in the English Premier League through 10 matches this season.

'When you finish the game, you start in your mind to think about different things,' Pochettino mentioned after the win. 'Of course, it's tough because it's emotional. Because I really love these guys, and I love the players. I love the staff. I love the fans and everything.'.

Industry observers note that following the win, Pochettino was scheduled to fly from northern Kentucky to Manchester aboard a private plane chartered by his new club. The quick escape offered the chance to avoid major airlines following Friday's chaotic nationwide shutdown, and perhaps a few hours' sleep for a 54-year-old starting his new job on Wednesday at Carrington Training Centre.

Pochettino spent two years with the USMNT, helping to rebuild an attack around Pulisic.

Pochettino hugs a staff member prior to the CONCACAF Nations League Quarterfinal match.

Pochettino paces along a near-empty sideline after much of his staff left for Manchester.

And Pochettino didn't initiative on traveling alone.

Outgoing USMNT first-team coach Miguel D'Agostino, strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya and analyst Alec Scott were expected to join Pochettino aboard the flight to Manchester, where assistant Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez as well as Pochettino's son and fitness coach Sebastiano have already begun preparing for Sunday's matchup with Liverpool at Anfield.

Recent findings suggest that the quick turnaround means Pochettino will be able to work with the players as they begin reporting back from international duty. Furthermore, he is expected to speak to club media before conducting his pre-match press conference around lunchtime on Friday.

The Argentine national is replacing Michael Carrick at Old Trafford on a two-and-a-half year contract after United agreed to pay more than £10million ($13m) to buy him and his backroom staff out of their contracts with the US Soccer Federation.

Before boarding his flight, Pochettino not only waved to his adoring fans, but took a photo with staff and players on the pitch in Cincinnati.

'It's impossible not to cry, but that is because we care about the people and the people care about us,' he told reporters. 'When that happens, it's normal to show your emotions, no? Because we are human. We are no robots.'.

Mauricio Pochettino saying his final goodbyes to the USA fans as he's now gonna fly to Manchester immediately ❤️ pic.twitter.com/sCe8LCjpK5.

Pulisic, perhaps Pochettino's brightest pupil, scored on a bicycle kick in the 25th minute.

Pulisic celebrates his goal on Tuesday night in Cincinnati during the win over Haiti.

Pochettino was expected to board a flight from northern Kentucky to Manchester after the win.

Pochettino had been on something of a farewell tour in the US, where he embraced the local sports scene over his brief tenure. In between overseeing his final games with the USMNT, Pochettino was spotted at the Cincinnati Bengals' win over the visiting Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday.

The manager, sporting his blue USSF coat, was captured standing on the sidelines with members of his staff ahead before kickoff, where he mingled with Bengals special teamers such as kicker Evan McPherson, long snapper William Wagner and punter Ryan Rehkow.

A night earlier, Pochettino guided the US to a 6-0 win over Haiti in Miami to give his team a safe cushion for his farewell on Tuesday in Cincinnati.

Pochettino broke down in tears as he confirmed his decision last week, while admitting he couldn't turn down the 'dream' job with Manchester United.

Mauricio Pochettino walks on the field after the CONCACAF Nations League Quarterfinal.

American fans give Pochettino a standing ovation in Cincinnati after his farewell match.

Flanked by US Soccer Federation bosses at the team's headquarters in Georgia, an emotional Pochettino wiped away tears as he thanked the players and staff.

Industry observers note that 'I haven't prepared a speech, I'm talking with my heart,' he stated. 'It's difficult for me to talk now because I am a very emotional guy.

'I think it was one of the most difficult decisions of our career, but you have to move forward.

Recent findings suggest that 'Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives.

Industry observers note that 'In some part it's a very sad decision, in another part we are professional and we are trying to make our dreams come true. We are excited for that step forward.'.

United will pay the US Soccer Federation more than $13.2 million (£10m) in compensation for Pochettino and his backroom staff.

'I never noted I wanted to go back in the Premier League,' Pochettino, a former Tottenham, Chelsea and Southampton boss, told reporters last week. 'All of this was so quick because we arrived here last Friday and on Sunday afternoon this type of situation started to appear.'.

Pochettino turns his attention to an 18th-place United squad that has just one EPL win.

Mauricio Pochettino insisted it was the 'most difficult decision' to leave the USMNT.

Recent findings suggest that pochettino put together a 23-12-2 record with the US, while 78 players earned caps for the US over his tenure. Remarkably, nine teenagers made their USMNT debuts for Pochettino, including Hall, who scored on Tuesday.

According to recent reports, but the Americans failed to crack into the sport's upper echelon during Pochettino's brief tenure in the US. In his lone World Cup appearance with the team last summer, Pochettino guided the USMNT to the Round of 16, where the Americans fell to Belgium, 4-1.

That result was an improvement on 2018, when the US failed to qualify, but not on 2022, when then-coach Gregg Berhalter's similarly team fell short of the quarters with a 3-1 loss to the Netherlands.

Despite this, Pochettino's American players have remained largely supportive of his tenure, including Berhalter's son Sebastian, who said the outgoing coach helped him 'develop as a player and as a person.'.

Prior to Tuesday's win, Pochettino thanked American fans for the support he received over his two years with the national team.

Industry observers note that 'Thank you so much from the bottom of my heart for all the fans, for all the people that was supporting us in the last two years,' Pochettino said in a video posted on social media. 'Special, great memories of the World Cup and everything that we lived together. Always in my heart, always one of you. All the best and I wish everything good for the future.'.

Potential candidates to replace Pochettino in the US include former Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola, ex-England manager Gareth Southgate and some lesser-known candidates like Cherundolo, who now guides the United States U-23 team.

In a recent development, 'For us to win, we need to be great at a lot of things, and we need someone who cares about youth development, cares about our youth national team programs, our relationships with our clubs and the success of the federation more broadly,' US Soccer CEO JT Batson told TNT Sports on Tuesday. 'We know that is a key part of our success, and it's also a key part of how we've been able to attract great people because they get to do massive things.'.

Victims of Nazi war in Poland call on Germany for support

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1037 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • "We can no longer wait," declared Polish victims' organizations in a dramatic appeal to German civil society, published on November 5 on the website of the Foundation for Polish–German Reconciliation.
  • Sources indicate that "Around 50,000 survivors of Nazi persecution during the German occupation still live in Poland today.
  • Recent findings suggest that the open letter pointed out that many of the survivors are over 90 years old, struggling with illness and rising costs, and in need of help in their daily lives.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"We can no longer wait," declared Polish victims' organizations in a dramatic appeal to German civil society, published on November 5 on the website of the Foundation for Polish–German Reconciliation.

Sources indicate that "Around 50,000 survivors of Nazi persecution during the German occupation still live in Poland today. They include former concentration camp and prison inmates, people deported to Germany for forced labor and those subjected to other forms of Nazi repression," wrote the signatories of the appeal.

Recent findings suggest that the open letter pointed out that many of the survivors are over 90 years old, struggling with illness and rising costs, and in need of help in their daily lives. "For many, any further delay in deciding to provide assistance means that help will come too late," stated the appeal, which was distributed in German, Polish and English.

While Germany has recognized its moral responsibility toward the remaining survivors of Nazi persecution, the signatories pointed out that a corresponding decision on possible reparations by the German federal government has yet to be made.

Sources indicate that "Today, we appeal primarily to German civil society to provide humanitarian support to survivors of Nazi persecution living in Poland," they wrote, addressing businesses, foundations, associations and private citizens. "Every donation matters.".

The unresolved glitch of war reparations has clouded German-Polish relations for decades.

According to recent reports, following the 1989 democratic transition in Central and Eastern Europe and the reunification of Germany, the federal government provided 500 million deutschmarks to Holocaust victims in Poland. More than 1 million people received support through these funds. Former forced laborers also received payments from the EVZ Foundation, which works to preserve the memory of the victims of National Socialist persecution.

However, given the scale of German crimes during World War II, the reparations provided to date have been considered as insufficient by large parts of Polish society. German occupation policy in Poland was characterized by systematic crimes against the Polish population. An estimated 6 million Polish citizens were killed during the war, including about 3 million Polish Jews.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to recent reports, as part of the "General Plan East," a large portion of the population was to be displaced, enslaved or murdered. As early as 1939, the "Intelligenzaktion" specifically targeted the Polish elites, including teachers, clergy, civil servants and intellectuals. In addition, approximately 2.5 million Poles were deported to the German Reich for forced labor and made to work there under inhumane conditions.

When it came to power in 2015, Poland's right-wing conservative Law and Justice Party (PiS)  made the problem of war reparations a central focus of Warsaw's policy toward Berlin. The PiS government estimated Poland's war losses at 6.2 trillion zloty (approx. €1.3 trillion/$1.58 trillion) and officially demanded this sum from Berlin in October 2022.

Industry observers note that the center-left government led by Donald Tusk has distanced itself from these demands since Tusk's election victory in December 2023. However, the government has also made no secret of the fact that Poland is expecting a "creative solution" from its German partner, according to Foreign Minister Radek Sikorski.

Former German Chancellor Olaf Scholz had offered €200 million ($224 million) prior to his visit to Poland in the summer of 2024, an offer rejected by Tusk as insufficient. The talks held since then between Berlin and Warsaw have failed to produce a solution.

In a final declaration following the German-Polish government consultations in December 2025, the German government promised to "analyze possibilities for additional support for Polish victims of Nazi aggression and the German occupation of Poland.".

"At the moment, there is no decision regarding a humanitarian gesture and the draft budget reflects this status," Josef Hinterseher, deputy spokesperson for Germany's Federal Foreign Office, told reporters on September 23.

Germany's opposition Greens party has not given up hope of a turnaround in its efforts to secure a "humanitarian gesture.".

"Our parliamentary group submitted a request to the budget committee to secure funding for this 'humanitarian gesture.' Unfortunately, the request was rejected," Franziska Brantner, co-chair of the Greens, told DW on Thursday in Warsaw.

"Hope dies last, so we will do everything in our power to ensure that the coalition makes this change after all," she emphasized. Brantner sees the budget committee's "final review session," which will take place this week, as a last chance.

The problem of reparations still plays an important role in Polish society, even more than 80 years after the end of the war. There is hardly a family that did not suffer during the war. In the latest German-Polish Barometer — a representative survey that has been conducted for 25 years — 53% of respondents stated that the suffering of the Polish people is not sufficiently acknowledged in Germany. Only 18% believed that the Germans have done enough.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Jakub Deka, chairman of the Foundation for Polish–German Reconciliation, believes the appeal by the victims' associations could now mobilize Germany's civil society. Following an initial appeal in May directed at the German federal government, several hundred Germans responded with donations ranging from €50 to several hundred euros.

Recent findings suggest that to date, a total of more than €35,000 ($39,000) has been deposited into the foundation's account. Several people in need have already received one-time assistance from this fund. "It's a drop in the bucket, but every little bit helps," Deka told DW.

The foundation's chairman quotes Jerzy Tarasiewicz — who led the victims' association in the Polish city of Gdansk for many years — as a cautionary reminder. In January, Tarasiewicz was quoted in an interview with the daily newspaper Gazeta Wyborcza as saying: "They [the Germans] are waiting for us to die.".

Tarasiewicz, who was born in 1942 on a German farm where his parents were performing forced labor, died in late September at the age of 84 without being able to witness this "humanitarian gesture.".

"It is a painful reminder that the victims cannot wait any longer," said Deka.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Two children died from gene therapies in China: where the field goes next.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Credit: Victor Habbick Visions/SPL.

In a recent development, chinese authorities have sacked the researcher who led an experimental gene-editing trial that resulted in the death of a child. An investigation into the trial by the Shanghai municipal government found that the researcher and his team failed to follow regulations and overlooked warning signs in a safety report. Several others involved in the case have also been punished.

Two children died from gene therapies in China: where the field goes next.

Two children died from gene therapies in China: where the field goes next.

Recent findings suggest that in July, the journal Science and the website Retraction Watch jointly reported that Zilong Qiu, a neuroscientist at Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine, led a team that developed an experimental gene-editing therapy for a six-year-old girl with a rare neurodevelopmental disorder called Snijders Blok–Campeau syndrome. The therapy was carried by a viral vector that was injected into the girl’s spine and then travelled to her brain. The girl died of medical complications after receiving the therapy at Xinhua Hospital, also in Shanghai, in March 2025.

Recent findings suggest that the institutions involved in the trial — Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine and Xinhua Hospital — have also been reprimanded and instructed to examine their own practices. “I expect the action to send a major warning to research institutes and hospitals across the country,” says Jiayou Shi, a lawyer at the National Research Center for Civil and Commercial Law at Renmin University of China in Beijing.

The trial was conducted under China’s fast-track pathway, called investigator-initiated trials (IITs). IITs allow researchers and biotech companies to test therapies promptly in hospitals without supervision from the country’s regulators. The Chinese government increased oversight of these trials in May, which Shi says should prevent similar cases in future.

Lizzi Lee, who studies China’s economic and technological policies at the Asia Society Policy Institute, a think tank in Latest York City, says the trial is “a cautionary tale” for the country’s rapidly growing biotechnology industry. There is real momentum in the industry in China, but clinical oversight hasn’t always kept pace, Lee says. “The investigation is quite candid about what went wrong,” adds Lee.

According to recent reports, according to a statement released through China’s state-run media on 13 November, the Shanghai government’s investigation found that Qiu was the main person responsible for the research. He has been sacked from his position as the deputy director of the Songjiang Research Institution, which is affiliated with Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine. Another member of Qiu’s team, a deputy researcher at Xinhua Hospital, has also been dismissed. Both researchers have been barred from leading or participating in science projects for five years and have been added to a national database of people and organizations that have committed serious breaches of research integrity.

About a month before the girl received the experimental therapy, Qiu’s team received results from a preclinical toxicology study showing that monkeys sustained liver damage, according to Science and Retraction Watch. Investigators found that Qiu’s team failed to inform the researcher in charge of the clinical research at Xinhua Hospital in a timely fashion about the results of the primate experiment, which meant “the early warning signal” in the safety report was not “given high attention”, according to the statement. The clinical researcher has been removed as head of research at Xinhua Hospital. Qiu did not respond to questions about the investigation report.

Shi says the trial in the girl should not have gone ahead if the therapy showed evidence of harm in animals.

It has been revealed that the investigators also found that Xinhua Hospital failed to conduct sufficient scientific assessment for the clinical trial. According to the statement, although the hospital’s ethics committee asked the research team to submit extra materials when safety evidence was lacking, it approved the trial without receiving those materials. In addition, the consent form given to the children’s family did not mention death as a risk of taking the therapy. Two members of the hospital’s ethics committee were given penalties.

Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine and Xinhua Hospital did not respond to questions about the investigation report.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

So where do Manchester United go from here? It is never a good look when opposition fans start willing a rival club to stick with their manager, but that was the ignominy that had befallen Michael Carrick by the end of an afternoon in which Lisandro Martinez’s latest plastic hardman impression embodied the very worst of United’s self-sabotage.

After seeing their team go 2-0 up when Cole Palmer converted the penalty given away by Martinez’s lunacy, the Chelsea fans taunted Carrick with chants of “You’re getting sacked in the morning” and later “You’re going down with the City”, a nod to the other Manchester club who are crisis torn for very different reasons.

As the final whistle loomed, though, and with United just grateful Estevao had not punished Martinez’s red card more severely, the Chelsea fans had changed their tune. “Michael Carrick, we want you to stay,” came the chant from the Matthew Harding Stand and that cut far deeper.

And to think that the opening 45 minutes had offered United and their fans some hope of a little respite from the storm before ultimately giving way to an ever-darkening gloom.

Industry observers note that carrick, who had been given a stay of execution in midweek, stated he still expected to be in charge for Roma’s visit to Old Trafford on Tuesday in the Champions League. But it is hard to escape the feeling that another managerial change will be coming at United before too long even if no one can be sure what happens next.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After England ended Spain's 43-game unbeaten run, which was the longest in international men's football history, with their 3-2 win, Thomas Tuchel's side secured the top spot in their UEFA Nations League group, and will soon find out who they'll face in the quarter-finals.

As the draw takes place, eight of Europe's biggest nations will be paired up for two-legged ties in March, with a place at June's finals at stake. Portugal, France and Spain have all won the trophy, but we could see a new champion crowned in 2027.

Here's when the draw takes place, who's in it and how to watch.

The draw for the quarter-finals of the Nations League will take place at the UEFA headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland on Friday 20th November at 12:00 local time, or 11:00 GMT.

As well as finding out the match-ups for the quarter-finals, viewers will also find out who will face who in the promotion and relegation playoffs between Leagues A/B and B/C.

Recent findings suggest that the first leg will take place between 25th-27th March 2027, during the March international break, with the return fixture kicking-off just days later, between 28th and 30th March. The four winners will go through to the Nations League Finals. Semi-final pairings will be established by another draw, with the losers taking a spot in the third-placed playoff, and the winners booking themselves a place in the final.

As winners of their group, England earned themselves a seeded spot in the draw, alongside France, Germany and Portugal, with the latter having won the tournament twice, including the most recent edition in 2024/25 when they beat Spain on penalties.

The unseeded side of the pot is made up of nations who finished as runners-up of their respective groups, namely Belgium, the Netherlands, Spain and Norway, who will play in their first ever Nations League Finals.

Recent findings suggest that winning their group ensured that England achieved a seeded spot in the draw. This means that they cannot face one of the other nations who won their group. A seeded spot also means that England will play the second-leg of the quarter-finals at home, which could play a significant role should they need a result.

England also cannot be drawn against anyone from their own group, meaning that a rematch against Spain is out of the question until the semi-finals. This leaves England's potential quarter-final opponents as Belgium, the Netherlands or Norway.

Fans can still follow the draw in real-time by tuning in for free to UEFA TV, or by watching on UEFA's official YouTube channel.

Sources indicate that UEFA's official broadcast partners will also cover the draw in one form or another, with ITV, BBC and Sky Sports being useful networks for those based in the UK. In the USA, UEFA Nations League is shown on FOX Sports, Fubo and ViX.

Former Man United boss Michael Carrick was seen enjoying some time out of the spotlight as he watched The Courteeners at a gig in London over the weekend.

Carrick, 45, was relieved of his duties as United boss on Thursday following a dismal start to the season that has seen his former side pick up just eight points and one victory in ten matches.

That came despite his incredible impact in the second half of last season when he replaced Ruben Amorim and led the Red Devils to third place in the Premier League.

And on Saturday night, a few days after his tenure ended, Carrick attended a tour date of The Courteeners.

According to the band's schedule, they were performing at Alexandra Palace in London.

One fan shared a photo on X from the gig, with the caption 'One hell of a day out'.

Michael Carrick was spotted watching The Courteneers at a gig in London over the weekend (Source X/adamkearey).

In the shot, Carrick looked relaxed and was smiling as he tried to make the most of a rare Saturday off.

The Courteeners were formed in Manchester and their frontman Liam Fray is known to be a lifelong United fan.

He regularly shared praise for Carrick during his time in the Old Trafford dugout, including backing him to get the best out of Marcus Rashford on his return to the club after his loan spell at Barcelona.

Some of The Courteeners' most famous songs include Are You In Love With A Notion? and Not Nineteen Forever, ironically the position United were in under Carrick until their 96th-minute equaliser against Aston Villa before the international break took them up to 18th place.

Following his sacking on Thursday after ten months in charge, Carrick issued a heartfelt statement reflecting on his tenure.

Posting on social media, he said: ‘I’ve had the immense privilege of leading Manchester United, the football club that I love.

‘There are very few who get to live that and feel it, and for that I’m incredibly grateful. I want to say a massive thank-you to the supporters. I must say, you are a special, rare breed.

‘I know we’ve not had the results lately, but you’ve shown me nothing but love and support in times when the easiest thing, and what most end up doing, would be to turn the other way.

Industry observers note that ‘That’s what makes you who you are. That’s why I fell in love with this club all those years ago.’.

Carrick was relieved of his duties at Man United on Thursday after a dismal start to the season.

The axe ultimately fell on Carrick on Thursday, yet the writing was on the wall for several days beforehand as speculation spread and United's hierarchy worked towards an agreement with Mauricio Pochettino.

Many former United stars were hugely critical of their former club, with Gary Neville calling their treatment of Carrick 'disgusting', while Peter Schmeichel labelled it 'very disrespectful'.

Rio Ferdinand also compared United's 142-word statement announcing his sacking to 'like ChatGPT' after there was no comment added by club chiefs.

United are back in action on Sunday when they travel to Anfield to take on Liverpool in what will be Pochettino's first game in charge.

Industry observers note that behind every successful football team is a top-quality goalkeeper. Acting as the final barrier of defence, their crucial saves, last-minute heroics and composure in between the sticks can be the difference between success and failure.

Sources indicate that an outfield player can make a mistake and get away with it; a goalkeeper can't. As they play with hopes and dreams on their backs, they have to perform at the highest level every week.

Elite goalkeepers are capable of winning points almost single-handedly and the very best are often held in the highest regard by the clubs they've starred for.

Liverpool struggled with Loris Karius in goal during 2018, as the German made two crucial mistakes to see the Reds lose the Champions League final to Real Madrid. They bought Alisson Becker in the summer of 2018, helping them win the Champions League a year later. It showcases how crucial they are.

Recent findings suggest that to honour their efforts between the posts, here are the greatest goalkeepers of all time. Each player's selection and ranking has been carefully considered, using ranking factors which are outlined below.

According to recent reports, hugo Lloris was at the heart of Tottenham's modern-day 'golden era' from 2012 until 2024. He was their captain under manager Mauricio Pochettino, providing experience in the key matches. The Frenchman was a world-class goalkeeper season after season, with a string of penalty saves in the 2018/19 campaign helping Spurs secure Champions League football and reach the final.

However, he never won a trophy with the Lilywhites, unlike his time as France captain. Lloris became a world champion with Les Bleus in 2018, and he was unfortunate to miss out on a second World Cup winner's medal four years later. The former Tottenham captain was also a runner-up in the 2016 European Championships, but he was victorious in the 2020/21 UEFA Nations League. A stalwart between the posts for years, he went on to become his country's most-capped player, with manager Didier Deschamps hailing him as "exemplary" for his years of service.

OGC Nice, Lyon, Tottenham, LAFC.

According to recent reports, earning the nickname "the Iron Curtain," Rinat Dasayev made a name for himself with Spartak Moscow for remarkable saves. Spending most of his years at the Russian club in the 1980s, he was renowned for his one-handed stops and remarkable athleticism.

Dasayev was the Soviet Union's goalkeeper and captain during their impressive run to the finals of Euro 1988. He was a part of the side which beat England 3-1 to confirm the Three Lions' exit from the competition, but is arguably remembered most of all for being the 'keeper who was beaten in goal after Marco van Basten's stunning volley. Still, he'd been impressive enough at that tournament and throughout the year to be named the best goalkeeper in the world.

Volgar, Spartak Moscow, Sevilla.

Michel Preud'homme came through the ranks at Standard Liege, spending nine years with the Belgian club before going on to represent Mechelen and then Portuguese titans Benfica. Although he was only at the Eagles for the final five years of his career, he earned the name 'Saint Michel' by supporters for his heroics between the posts.

On the international stage, Preud'homme was equally impressive. Having been a back-up 'keeper during the Red Devils' run to the final of Euro 1980, he took centre stage at the 1990 and 1994 World Cups, ensuring his country reached the round of 16. That tournament also saw him bestowed with the inaugural Yashin Award for the best goalkeeper at the tournament.

Standard Liege, Mechelen, Benfica.

After coming through the ranks of Inter Milan and a series of loan moves to Salernitana, Savona and Sambenedettese, Walter Zenga was eventually given the opportunity to be the nerrazurri's number one. And he made the position his own for years before he departed the club in 1994.

It has been revealed that named the best goalkeeper in the world for three years, the Italian helped his side lift the Serie A in 1988/89, an impressive achievement considering how much of a powerhouse their rivals AC Milan were at that time. Also his country's first-choice shot-stopper, Zenga ensured Italy finished third at their home World Cup in 1990, repeating an achievement that the Azzurri managed at Euro 1988.

Inter Milan, Sampdoria, New England Revolution.

Notable Individual Achievements.

Peter Shilton is one of the best English goalkeepers ever. He is most well-known for his contribution to Nottingham Forest's two European Cup triumphs in 1979 and 1980. Brian Clough heralded Shilton as being even better than World Cup-winning goalkeeper Gordon Banks, as he also helped the East Midlands club secure the First Division title in 1978.

Shilton made 125 appearances for his country, playing in some high-profile World Cup matches, including the quarter-final against Argentina, where Diego Maradona scored the infamous 'Hand of God' goal past him. Although he was unable to secure a major tournament for the Three Lions, he holds the record for the most caps for his country.

Leicester City, Stoke City, Nottingham Forest, Southampton, Derby, West Ham.

Andoni Zubizarreta is a Spanish football legend, representing his country 126 times from 1985 to 1998. He played in seven major tournaments for his country, captaining his country to the 1994 and 1998 World Cups.

Zubizarretta also had an illustrious club career, playing for the likes of Barcelona, Valencia, and Athletic Bilbao. He won La Liga twice for the Basque side, including the league and cup double in the 1983/84 season, but his main success was in Catalonia. As a Barcelona player, Zubizarreta played an integral part in securing six La Liga titles, as well as the 1991/92 European Cup under the management of Johan Cruyff. The Spanish goalkeeper was ahead of his time in terms of his ability with the ball at his feet and ease under pressure.

Alaves, Athletic Bilbao, Barcelona, Valencia.

Recent findings suggest that in the annals of Spanish football, not many players have a legacy like Ricardo Zamora. Playing most of his football at Espanyol, he also featured for both Barcelona and Real Madrid during the 1920s and 30s, becoming one of La Roja's earliest football stars.

In 1930, Zamora was between the sticks as Spain became the first side outside the British Isles to beat England in a competitive match, playing with a broken sternum as his country ran out 4-3 victors. There is a common saying throughout Spain which underlines El Divino's incredible talent: "there are only two goalkeepers: Ricardo Zamora on Earth and St Peter in Heaven." Moreover, the goalkeeper with the lowest goals-to-game ratio in La Liga each season is now given the 'Zamora Trophy,' a testament to the goalkeeper's sporting legacy.

Espanyol, Barcelona, Real Madrid, OGC Nice.

Dino Zoff was an ever-present member of the Juventus and Italy teams throughout the 1970s. His most notable achievement is undoubtedly his 1982 World Cup triumph for the Azzurri, where he captained the side to glory. After finishing runner-up in 1970, it was looking as if Zoff would go his whole career without a World Cup triumph, but 1982 saw the legendary goalkeeper win the trophy at the age of 40.

GIVEMESPORT Key Statistic: Dino Zoff is the oldest player to win the World Cup.

At club level, he was even more successful, winning six Serie A titles as well as two Coppa Italia titles and a UEFA Cup. Hailed as a "legend" by shot-stopper Gianluigi Buffon, the only thing that Zoff didn't tick off his resume was the European Cup. He was a runner-up in 1973 and a decade later, when Juventus lost to Hamburger SV.

Udinese, Mantova, Napoli, Juventus.

Although most football supporters will name Pele or Garrincha first when asked about Brazil's World Cup-winning squads of 1958 and 1962, Gilmar was an equally vital cog in the machinery. Arguably one of the best goalkeepers of the 20th century, he was the last line of defence for two of the Selecao's most famous triumphs on the international stage, conceding just four times in their 1958 success.

According to recent reports, along with his 93 caps for the national side, Gilmar was a key presence for both Corinthians and Santos during the 1950s and 60s. His calmness between the sticks saw him win multiple pieces of silverware, particularly with the latter, as he collected five Serie A titles, along with two Copa Libertadores.

Neville Southall began his career in English football at Bury in 1980, before joining Everton a year later. Southall spent 17 years at the Merseyside club, winning two league titles, two FA Cups, and the 1984/85 European Cup Winners' Cup. He remains the all-time record appearance holder for the Toffees and is still renowned as one of the best players in the club's history.

According to recent reports, in the 1980s, Southall was well-recognised as the best goalkeeper in English football, with Jamie Carragher even naming him the best goalkeeper ever. In the 1984/85 title-winning campaign, Southall picked up the Football Writers' Association Footballer of the Year. He also made 92 appearances for Wales, making his debut on 27th May 1982.

Bury, Everton, Port Vale, Stoke City, Torquay, Bradford.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A man from Trinidad and Tobago has won a legal appeal lasting almost a decade in the last court of appeal available to him — the judicial committee of the Privy Council in former colonial power Britain.

Jason Jones, a gay man born in Trinidad and Tobago, had challenged the Caribbean nation's Sexual Offences Act outlawing consensusal sex between adult males, saying that it breached his fundamental rights under the country's constitution.

He initially won his case at Trinidad and Tobago's High Court, but the government and religious organizations managed to partially overturn the ruling once more, prompting Jones to the take the case to the island nation's highest appellate authority — the Privy Council in  the UK.

"To discriminate against somebody simply because of who they choose to love is simply ridiculous," Jones told the Associated Press after Tuesday's judgment was rendered.

The Privy Council in London is the final court of appeal for some Commonwealth countries including Trinidad and Tobago, although that concern was already contentious in some circles prior to Tuesday's ruling.

A panel of five judges unanimously allowed Jones' appeal, dismissing a counter-appeal from the Caribbean country's Attorney General.

It found that two sections of the country's Sexual Offenses Act 1986, criminalizing "buggery" and "serious indecency" respectively among same-sex couples, violated Jones' fundamental rights to private and family life set out in the 1976 constitution.

The court wrote in its ruling that "the rights and interests of Mr Jones which are at stake involve a particularly important facet of his existence and identity since the ability to form an intimate and loving relationship with another person lies at the core of the right to private and family life.".

The anti-gay laws that call for up to five years in prison have not been enforced in recent history, but critics say they still send an intimidating message.

Judge Philip Sales said as he unveiled the ruling that "the current understanding of the fundamental individual right to respect for private and family life is that it protects such a core part of human identity as one's sexual orientation.".

Sales added that "laws which seek to criminalize such activities cannot be justified.".

Trinidadian authorities argued that because the 1986 laws were passed with a super-majority and constituted criminal penalties that dated back to colonial times, prior to the constitution, they could be considered "existing law" and override the individual constitutional rights in certain circumstances.

But the Privy Council judges found that the so-called "proviso" for this special status — "unless the Act is shown not to be reasonably justifiable in a society that has proper respect for the rights and freedoms of the individual" — had not been met.

One of Jones' lawyers, Anand Ramlogan, is a former attorney general of Trinidad and Tobago and argued against this position earlier in the case.

"Constitutional rights exist precisely because majorities are not always right," Ramlogan stated. "They ensure that the dignity and equality of every citizen are not left to the changing tides of public opinion.".

Jason Jones is a 61-year-old born in Trinidad and Tobago.

Openly gay since the age of 16, he remarked he fled the country in 1996 because of homophobic violence and discrimination.

Speaking to the Associated Press on Tuesday after what he termed a "stunning victory," he remarked he would describe himself as a "very angry gay man," whose anger had helped him persist in his legal appeal for so many years.

"Society has treated me worse than a criminal," he mentioned. "There is a real sense of vindication with this judgment. Finally, the courts are seeing that they need to step up because our politicians are so toothless.".

He mentioned he became inspired to speak out after losing friends to HIV/AIDS and after meeting American singer-songwriter Nina Simone when she toured the island nation for three weeks in 1984, when he was 19.

"Nina was the one who said, 'Jason, get off this rock and go see the world,'" he said, calling it a defining and life-changing experience.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Trinidad and Tobago's government, the country's Council of Evangelical Churches and its largest Hindu organization, Sanatan Dharm Maha Sabha, contested the case, which has wound its way through several courts since the appeal was debuted in 2017.

In 2018, Trinidad's High Court found the laws unconstitutional. But in 2025, a local appeals court partially reversed the ruling. Trinidad's Court of Appeals subsequently allowed Jones to seek a ruling from the final appeals court in England.

The case was being closely watched by activists across the Caribbean, with similar laws in place in several other countries in the region.

The Bahamas decriminalized homosexuality in 1991.

The UK repealed laws in overseas territories Anguilla, the British Virgin Islands, the Cayman Islands, Montserrat and the Turks and Caicos Islands in 2001.

It has been revealed that judges in Barbados, Dominica, St. Lucia and Antigua and Barbuda have also recently struck down similar laws.

According to recent reports, but in former British colonies Grenada, Jamaica, Trinidad and Tobago and St. Vincent and the Grenadines it remains a crime.

The UK only decriminalized gay sex in 1967, more than four centuries after the so-called "buggery" laws were first introduced under King Henry VII, and more than a century after the last executions for the crime. People still faced prosecution or the threat of it for consensual adult gay sex until after World War II, with surely the most famous later-years case being that of computing and codebreaking pioneer and war hero Alan Turing.

Arsenal are reportedly set to hold contract talks with Martin Odegaard and Riccardo Calafiori next after recently agreeing a flurry of fresh deals.

It’s been widely reported that Declan Rice, Jurrien Timber, Piero Hincapie, and David Raya have all agreed upcoming contracts with the Gunners.

And now Football Transfers adds that Odegaard and Calafiori could be next for Arsenal as they plan further negotiations to tie down their star names.

Odegaard is Arsenal captain and it’s surely particularly crucial to ensure the Norway international’s future is settled as soon as possible after some recent speculation over his future.

Sky Germany recently reported on Arsenal hoping to tie Odegaard down to a upcoming deal as Bayern Munich could be a threat to their hopes of keeping their skipper.

The 27-year-old is a world class playmaker on his day, and it’s easy to imagine him shining for other major European clubs such as Bayern.

Still, Bayern expert Christian Falk recently reported that he didn’t consider Odegaard moving to Allianz Arena as particularly likely or realistic at this moment in time, so that’s hopeful for Arsenal.

It’s also vital for AFC to keep hold of Calafiori, who could surely be another of their stars to attract interest from Europe’s elite.

The 24-year-old defender has shone since moving to the Emirates Stadium, and despite some problems with injuries, he looks like he has the potential to keep on improving and contributing to the team’s success.

Calafiori has been linked with Real Madrid in recent times, while Simon Phillips has reported on Chelsea also being suitors for the Italy international.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, en route to their second NWSL championship in two years, relatively latest Gotham FC recruit Jaedyn Shaw was uninterested in the narratives that underestimated her team. The surprise win at the NWSL Shield-winning Kansas City Current in the playoff quarterfinals was not a surprise to her, and she made it clear with three quick words: "Underdog, my ass.".

It has been revealed that shaw had a point on that cold day in the Midwest, and almost exactly a year later, it still stands. Gotham are the NWSL's new dynasty, and their Shield win marked their fifth major title in three years, with a sixth in their sights as the playoffs begin this weekend. The transformation was rapid for a team that has historically been a bottom-dweller, so much so that their 2023 championship triumph was a genuine surprise. They quickly built a title-winning team and reaped the rewards just as swiftly, but even as the muscle memory of title charges returns, Gotham will go about their next NWSL playoff journey differently. The target is officially on their backs, the onus officially on them to live up to the billing.

Industry observers note that gotham have played the vast majority of their playoff games as the lowest-seeded team in the postseason, winning the championship twice in those circumstances. Sunday's quarterfinal against the Seattle Reign, though, will be the first game they play as the unquestionable favorites to win the whole thing. How Gotham will play with the weight of expectations is entirely unclear, since they have never done it before, but it is a good problem of their own creation, one they have chased since the 2023 triumph.

Date: Sunday, Nov. 8 | Time: 12:30 p.m. ETLocation: Sports Illustrated Stadium -- Harrison, N.J.TV: ABC | Live stream: ESPN AppOdds: Gotham FC -150; Draw +265; Seattle Reign +340.

Sources indicate that their blitz in the free-agent market in the winter of 2024 laid the foundation for their dynastic run, but the most fascinating feature of Gotham's years-long run of success is the evolution they have undergone since. U.S. women's national team defender Tierna Davidson has become the team's captain, her progressive passing ability making her a key fixture in head coach Juan Carlos Amoros' system. Her club and country teammate Rose Lavelle has become a standout, but the star of the show has been Shaw, who has barely missed a beat since her arrival in September 2025.

In a recent development, shaw has 14 goals and seven assists in 35 NWSL games with Gotham, her wide-ranging skill set fully on display in Amoros' team. She has been a little bit of everything for the team's attack, which is arguably too reliant on her talents, but it is almost hard to fault Amoros for the approach. The system has allowed Shaw to flourish, in particular bringing out a clear goal-scoring quality that is key to a Gotham team that values defensive work rate first.

Sources indicate that "First, I think the commitment they have to defend and the commitment they have to work hard for the team despite being some of the best players technically in the planet," Amoros stated about both Shaw and Lavelle after a win over the Chicago Stars in September. "I think that helps the connection, not only between them two. There is a mutual respect there because of that but then also from the whole team. When you have to play and those are the players that produce the chances for us in the final third but then the people that [are] behind them are always supportive of them because of the work they put in and then we try to work a lot with them to how we can find them and how they can connect more with each other and the same with Sam [Kerr].".

He has found a unique way to make Shaw and Lavelle work together, despite the fact that they appear to have overlapping skill sets when it comes time for USWNT head coach Emma Hayes to slot them into her lineup. The pair often play just behind Kerr, an out-and-out striker, and assume the role of strikers themselves while balancing their creative tendencies. They have filled in some gaps along the way -- Kerr, for example, ranks third in the league with 9.67 expected goals since returning to the NWSL on July 16 but has scored just four times. Kerr does, though, have four assists in 17 games, one fewer than Shaw and one more than Lavelle over that span.

The connection between Lavelle and Shaw has offered Gotham a level of dynamism that has been missing in their attack at times over the years, even as they racked up title after title. It helps that the two have enjoyed working alongside each other, the 21-year-old Shaw in particular taking inspiration from Lavelle, a decade her senior.

"I think her movement is some of the best in the world, honestly," Shaw mentioned after that September win over the Stars. "She's able to make stretch runs, drag players. She attracts so many players, opening up space for other players to get on the ball and then getting on the second one, I think, is one of her strengths and is something I'm trying to replicate off of her. I think she's just incredibly smart in soccer knowledge.".

It has been revealed that for each of them, a return to fitness after small injuries in the final weeks of the regular season comes not a moment too soon. Kerr's inconsistency is not the only attacking issue they will need to overcome -- Jordyn Dudley will miss the postseason with a foot fracture she sustained last month, her impressive rookie season coming to a close with four goals and three assists. Lavelle and Shaw will be particularly useful against the Reign, whose defensive qualities continue to be a strength.

In a recent development, shaw has become the focal point of Gotham's reinvention in recent years, but Amoros' side has added experienced options in a wide variety of positions since the 2023 championship. The vast majority of Gotham's likely starters on Sunday will have joined the club after the 2023 playoff run, a steady stream of crucial players signing themselves up since. Ann-Katrin Berger, the 2024 goalkeeper of the year, made the move not long after Davidson and Lavelle did, and European champion Jess Carter followed right after. Midfielder Jaelin Howell, who has been in and around the USWNT, was recruited in time for the 2025 season, and Shaw joined months later. Left back Guro Reiten has two goals and six assists since making her club debut in April, while Kerr made the move at roughly the same time as midfielder Denise O'Sullivan, a two-time NWSL champion with the North Carolina Courage.

Gotham's reinvention is constant, the core evolving each and every season. It is a unique route to the top, but in another season of change, they found the consistency they have been chasing since the 2023 championship. The underdog label has well and truly been shed, the team chasing another tag entirely -- a third championship would put them level with the Portland Thorns as the most successful team in the league's history.

Sources indicate that it is hardly a surprise to learn that Gabriel, who sports the name 'Gabriel Jr' on his shirt, is strongly supported and influenced by his father, who has been a vocal advocate throughout his career, including — to the chagrin of some — on social media. It is fair to say that the player's father occupies a significant role in his career.

Here, GIVEMESPORT brings you all you need to know about JJ Gabriel's father.

Joe O'Cearuill (sometimes written Ó Cearúill) is the father of JJ Gabriel. Born in north London on February 9, 1987, O'Cearuill was a professional footballer whose career spanned around 12 years and saw him play for clubs across England and Ireland.

His football CV includes clubs such as Arsenal, Watford, Brighton, Barnet and Forest Green Rovers, as well as full international honours with the Republic of Ireland.

Edmonton, North London, England.

Arsenal, Brighton, Forest Green Rovers, Republic of Ireland.

O'Cearuill was a defender during his career, featuring in the centre-back and right-back positions - a stark contrast to his son, who is very much an attacker inspired by the likes of Messi and Ronaldo, two of the greatest football players of all time.

According to recent reports, though born in England, O'Cearuill has links to Trinidad and Tobago through his father and Ireland through his mother, whose connection is to the south-western county of Cork. These connections benefit his son, who is eligible for a number of countries as a result.

JJ Gabriel's real full name is Joseph Junior Andreou O'Cearuill. According to reports, his name was changed in a bid to make it more marketable.

O'Cearuill began his football journey in 2004 as a youth player for Leyton Orient before moving on to Watford and eventually earning a professional contract with Arsenal in 2006.

In a recent development, he played mostly for the Gunners' reserve teams, but trained with the first team and featured on the bench in a number of games. While on the books at Arsenal, he spent a brief spell on loan at Brighton, who were then playing in League One, and featured in a testimonial game for Dennis Bergkamp.

During his time as an Arsenal player, O'Cearuill earned call-ups to the Ireland Under-21 and senior squads. He made two senior appearances for the Boys in Green under Steve Staunton, playing in friendly games against Ecuador and Bolivia in the United States. The image above highlights him in action against Aaron Lennon and the England U-21s.

Came off the bench for Stephen O'Halloran on the 73rd minute and received a yellow card.

Started and played full 90 minutes alongside Alan Bennett at centre-back.

As well as playing for clubs across England, O'Cearuill had a short spell in Ireland with St Patrick's Athletic in 2008, which saw him play for the club in the UEFA Cup against the likes of Hertha Berlin.

In a recent development, O'Cearuill is generally perceived as a 'journeyman' footballer, due to the fact that he played for a large number of teams and spent relatively brief periods at each. He concluded his playing days in 2016 at Haringey Borough.
